source.citation: "Tremont House." Chicagology. Compiling city-directory entries 1846-1870, an uncredited building summary, Chicago Illustrated (January 1866) by James W. Sheahan, and a reader's letter headed "THE FOUR TREMONTS", Chicago Tribune, 2 February 1874.
what_it_does_not_supply: an independent storey count - the only one on the page is an uncredited modern summary sentence
any dimension, plan or roof form
the builder's name (Alanson Sweet is not on this page)
the first proprietor Starr Foot, or the 1835 sale to Mallory & Able
anything reliable in its header metadata block, which describes the later Tremonts
what_it_supplies: built 1833 at the north-west corner of Lake and Dearborn streets
frame / wooden construction, twice attested in period texts on the page
"a mere shell, without any sidewalk around it", poorly furnished, rooms not entirely carpeted, beds often without a pillow
Ira Couch became proprietor the year after it was built, i.e. 1834
the corner impassable to the stage in early spring, passengers walking some two blocks
destroyed by fire in the fall of 1839
kept by the Couch brothers (Chicago Illustrated, 1866)
